_about: Public-domain John Taylor of Norwich (1694-1761), Presbyterian Hebraist, for the Word Hoard: The Scripture Doctrine of Original Sin (1740) and A Paraphrase with Notes on the Epistle to the Romans (1745), from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 46 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

jtaylor-original-sin: The Scripture doctrine of original sin proposed to free and candid examination (London : Printed by J. Wilson, 1740)
jtaylor-romans: A paraphrase with notes on the Epistle to the Romans : to which is prefix'd a key to the apostolic writings, or an essay to explain the Gospel scheme, and the principal words and phrases the apostles have used in describing it (London : J. Waugh, 1745)

_excluded.jtaylor-other: The Hebrew Concordance (1754-1757), a reference work; the 1762 Scripture Account of Prayer
_excluded.jtaylor-not-his: IA scripturedoctrin00tayl_1 (catalogued under Taylor as The Scripture Doctrine of Atonement, 1809) is in fact Stephen West's Scripture Doctrine of Atonement, by its title page: the fetcher's name check caught the mis-cataloguing
